To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sciatic nerve irritation causes impairment of mitochondrially associated ATP production, which recovers within 14 day.
the sciatic nerve l ligation causes mitochondrial impairment of the spinal cord motor neurons in rats.
sciatic nerve CCI leads to mitochondrial clustering in the ipsilateral motor neurons of the L3-L6 spinal cord regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of mitochondrial impairment on the functional state of the respective motor neurons in spinal cord tissue.
the question of how the mitochondrial system responds to a peripheral nerve injury and how it contributes to the recovery process.
the question of how the mitochondrial system of spinal cord motor neuron responds to CCI of sciatic nerve.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mitochondrial function is impaired by CCI of the nerve.
the mitochondrial response to sciatic nerve liga- tion is complex and involves several mechanisms.
the observed mitochondrial changes are a consequence of the nerve injury and are not the cause of the nerve injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mitochondrial dysfunction is a key factor in CCI-induced pain.
CCI causes impairment of mitochondrion associated with changes in the distribution, respiration and cardiolipins.
CCI of the rat sciatic nerve causes a transient impairment of mitochondrial respiration in related motor neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondrial dysfunction is a major factor in the pathogenesis of neuropathic pain.
CCI of the peripheral nerve causes a complex response in spinal cord motor neurons with respect to the mitochondrial system.
mitochondrial function and cardiolipins are sensitive indicators of the pathogenesis of neuropathic pain.
